title: 5 Important Questions For Your Success
paragraphs: Most of us do not know our own purpose on Earth. So, I want to give you five questions to write down, which you must answer if you want to succeed on this planet. Five questions. Write it down. Don't forget it. These five questions are so important that they control the entire world. Everything a human being does on Earth is driven by these five questions. The poorest man who sleeps under a bridge tries to answer these five questions. The richest man living in the palace struggles with these five questions.

Every race, every creed, every ethnic group, and every culture grapples with these five questions. These five questions control the entire world. It actually creates the industry. These five questions create the world of fashion. These five questions shape the world of entertainment. These five questions are what wake you up every morning. These are the questions that produce corrupt leaders. These are the kinds of questions that produce people who abuse their own lives and the lives of others.

These five questions control politicians, heads of state, and prime ministers. These five questions control the priests. These five questions control the young people on the streets who sell their bodies. Because of these five questions, young people use drugs and engage in premarital relationships. These five questions are so powerful that they cause devastating wars in the world. What are these five questions? Number one, write it down. Who am I? Who am I? It's a difficult question to answer.

The second question that controls the human race is: Where am I from? Where did you come from? What is my source? Some people say you came from a monkey. Others say that you came from a salamander that crawled on a rock 6 million years ago and became a tadpole, then a frog, which also became a monkey and then a human. Some people believe that. The third question that every human being struggles with is: Why am I here? That's a difficult question. The average person does not know why he is on planet Earth.

They wake up every morning, go to a job they hate, work with people they don't like, are paid less than they deserve, and die young from frustration. Because they don't know why they exist. The fourth question that every human being must answer is: What can I do? Write it down. What can I do? The average person on Earth has no idea about their own abilities. 90% of the world's population will die without achieving more than 10% of their true potential. This is a tragedy.

The final question that every human being must answer is: Where am I going? What is my destination? Everyone wants to know, what is my future? Where will I be in the next twenty or forty years? Where will I be when I am seventy-five or eighty-two? What is my destiny? These five questions baffle humankind. These five questions changed my life. Because these five questions are the ones I couldn't answer. When I was thirteen years old, I began to read the Bible on my own. My father was a Baptist minister.

He was unable to help me answer those five questions. I went to church and became religious. But I didn't get an answer to any of the questions. So, I decided to look for the answers myself. I picked up the Bible at the age of thirteen. I was very young, a teenager, and I began reading the Book of Matthew. Matthew's book led me to Mark's book. Then I read the Book of Luke and memorized the Book of John, and my life completely exploded while I was a teenager.

I became like an adult before my time because I learned principles that even adults didn't know. By the time I turned seventeen, I was the most famous teenager in my country because of the Bible I had memorized. During those years I began to struggle with these five questions. Who am I? Where did you come from? Why am I here? What am I really capable of doing? Where am I going? I discovered that the greatest tragedy in life is not death. There is something worse than death.
The greatest tragedy in life is a life without purpose.
